title: Scripture: new creature, rebirth, Spirit renewal
source_text: VII. Rem autem ita se habere ex multis Scripturae locis evidenter colligitur. Et primo quidem ex eo quod fideles dicuntur novae creaturae, 2 Cor. 5. 17. Galat. 6. & Dei ποιημα, id est, factura, sive opus, Ephes. 2. 10. Item ex Deo nati, Joh. 1. 13. 1 Joh. 4. 7. & 5. 4. & quidem ita ut semen Dei manens in seipsis habeant, 1 Joh. 3. 9. A morte quoque peccati excitati & vivificati, ut deinceps per Spiritum vivant; Eph. 2. 5. Coloss. 2. 13. & denique, quod ipsis tribuitur renovatio per Spi-ritum Sanctum, Tit. 3. 5. Etenim his omnibus verbis & loquendi modis magna quaedam & totalis mutatio, virtute Spiritus Sancti in fidelibus effecta, designatur: mutatio, inquam, talis atque tanta, ut per eam novum quoddam esse, & novam quan-dam vitam acceperint: per quam, ut per aliquid ipsis insitum & immanens, distinguuntur a caeteris hominibus, qui ex carne tantum nati sunt, & in veteri statu ac morte peccati manent. Cum autem in fidelibus & regenitis idem esse Physicum & facultates eaedem maneant, nec in iis quicquam immutetur, quantum spectat ad hominis simpliciter consi-derati naturam atque essentiam; necesse omnino est mutationem illam moralem esse, & consistere in donis & habitibus sanctis, quibus Spiritus illos intus exornat, & ad recte pieque & juste agendum disponit.
pass_a_gloss: That the matter stands thus is clearly gathered from many places of Scripture. First, from the fact that believers are called new creatures (2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6), and God's workmanship or work (Ephesians 2:10); also born of God (John 1:13; 1 John 4:7 and 5:4), and that in such a way that they have God's seed remaining in themselves (1 John 3:9); raised and made alive from the death of sin so that thereafter they may live by the Spirit (Ephesians 2:5; Colossians 2:13); and finally that renovation by the Holy Spirit is ascribed to them (Titus 3:5). For by all these words and modes of speaking a great and total change wrought in believers by the power of the Holy Spirit is designated: a change, I say, such and so great that by it they have received a certain new being and a certain new life; by which, as by something implanted and immanent in them, they are distinguished from other men who are born of flesh alone and remain in the old state and death of sin. But since in believers and the regenerate the same physical being and the same faculties remain, and nothing is changed in them as regards the nature and essence of man simply considered, that change must altogether be moral and consist in holy gifts and habits with which the Spirit inwardly adorns them and disposes them to act rightly, piously, and justly.
pass_b_english: Scripture: new creature, God's workmanship, born of God, seed remaining, raised from sin's death, renewed by the Spirit.
Change is moral—holy habits disposing to right, pious, just action—not a change of physical essence.
